key_insight: Clifford disentanglers can reduce entanglement in molecular electronic-structure wavefunctions while preserving the Pauli-string Hamiltonian structure, making simulations more efficient without changing the problem representation.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical preconditioning layer for tensor-network and shallow quantum algorithms, improving accuracy at fixed resources and reducing sensitivity to orbital ordering and qubit mapping.
method: Classify Clifford operators by their effect on the Schmidt spectrum across a bipartition.
Shrink the search space to 20 two-qubit and 91,392 four-qubit representatives.
Embed the chosen Clifford transformations into an iterative Clifford-augmented MPS workflow and test in VQE settings.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports reduced energy errors at fixed bond dimension across molecular test cases, plus improved robustness to orbital-order and fermion-to-qubit mapping choices, and benefits in shallow-circuit VQE calculations.
watch_item: The approach depends on correlation structure, so gains may vary by molecule and the Clifford search/pruning overhead must be managed carefully in larger systems.
paper_title: Clifford disentanglers for entanglement reduction in molecular electronic structure simulations
